title: Commenting `//**` without a `*/` in Shader causes Editor to hang for significant durations
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.7.stable

### System information

Godot v4.7.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 4 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9621) - AMD Ryzen 7 9700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.16 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

After extensive debugging in a .gdshader in the Godot Shader Editor, I found the root cause of my editor (both shader editor, script editor and default editor) hanging, freezing and being unresponsive for long durations to be an incorrectly formatted [Documentation Comment](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/shaders/shader_reference/shading_language.html#comments). 

Rather than commenting 
```
/** This is a descriptor */
```
I had accidentally commented
```
//** This is a descriptor
```

with two slashes at the start of the comment and a missing escape/closing tag.

_The omission of the escape was a simple mistake, the two slashes mostly out of habit, since shaders, by default, require `//` for a comment._

When you have a **Node** selected in the editor that has the `ShaderMaterial` that uses the `shader` with a comment that is formatted like that, your editor will hang for 10s-1minute on every change. This only happens if the node is selected. This is likely because the `/**` is only read when the Inspector is opened, and the shader uniform descriptions are actually displayed.

There is no warning for this missing escape, and unlike with forgetting the escape with a normal Documentation Comment (`/**`), my shader did not become one large multi-line comment. Since even commenting out my entire shader did not resolve the issue, it was hard to find the source.

If either the editor had given an error for a missing escape (`/*` found, `*/` not found) or simply ignored the `/*`, since it was technically commented out, the issue would have not occurred, and either of those could be a solid fix. I presume the hanging is from the entire shader being read and attempted to be displayed as a descriptor, and therefore being a very extreme, but understandable slowdown.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a scene with Sprite3D (or other node that can handle a material), with a `ShaderMaterial` and a `shader` slotted in.
2. Somewhere in the shader, write `//** This will hang the editor`
3. Select the Node with the shader.
4. Any subsequent change to the shader or reselect of the Node will cause the editor to hang for a significant amount of time.

N/A
